Restore trailing zeros

Source: R/restore-zeros.R
restore_zeros.Rd

These functions are deprecated because the tests no longer take strings, so there is no need to restore trailing zeros for them. Give the number of decimal places as digits_x or digits_sd instead. To format numbers for display, use formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2).

restore_zeros() formats numbers as strings with a given number of decimal places, padding with zeros. By default, the target is the number of decimal places of the value that has the most. Do not rely on this default without checking it, since the value with the most decimal places may itself have lost trailing zeros.

restore_zeros_df() applies it to the columns of a data frame, by default all those coercible to numeric.

Usage

restore_zeros(
  x,
  width = NULL,
  sep_in = ".",
  sep_out = sep_in,
  check_width = c("capped", "never")
)

restore_zeros_df(
  data,
  cols = everything(),
  check_numeric_like = TRUE,
  check_decimals = FALSE,
  width = NULL,
  sep_in = ".",
  sep_out = sep_in,
  check_width = c("capped", "never")
)

Arguments

x

Numeric, or a string coercible to numeric. A value that is not coercible, such as "5%", becomes NA with a warning, and so does one with an exponent so large that it can't be written out, such as "1e-999999". A blank string or "NA" becomes NA without a warning.

width

Integer. Number of decimal places the output should have, up to 100,000. Length 1 or the length of x. Default is NULL, the largest number of decimal places in x.

sep_in

String. The separator between the integer part and the decimal places in the input, matched literally. Default is ".".

sep_out

String. The separator in the output. Default is sep_in.

check_width

String (length 1). What to do if a value has more decimal places than width? "capped" (the default) throws an error; "never" lets it pass.

data

Data frame or matrix. Only in restore_zeros_df().

cols

Columns to operate on, selected with tidyselect. Default is everything(), restricted by check_numeric_like. Only in restore_zeros_df().

check_numeric_like

Logical. If TRUE (the default), only columns that is_numeric_like() accepts are processed. A column that isn't numeric-like gets a warning if cols is given and selects it, or if it is processed anyway, unless it is empty. Only in restore_zeros_df().

check_decimals

Logical. If TRUE, columns without any decimal places are skipped. Default is FALSE. Only in restore_zeros_df().

Value

  • For restore_zeros(), a string vector.

  • For restore_zeros_df(), a data frame.

Details

Displayed numbers are often rounded, so a value may have more decimal places than it shows. x |> decimal_places() |> max() gives the actual maximum.

As in decimal_places(), numeric values with more than 15 significant digits cannot be padded accurately; enter such numbers as strings.

Examples

vec <- c(212, 75.38, 4.9625)

# By default, pad to the most decimal places in `vec`:
restore_zeros(vec)
#> Warning: `restore_zeros()` was deprecated in scrutiny 1.0.0.
#> ℹ Give the number of decimal places as `digits_x` or `digits_sd` instead. To
#>   format numbers for display, use `formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)`.
#> [1] "212.0000" "75.3800"  "4.9625"  

# Or to a given width:
restore_zeros(vec, width = 6)
#> [1] "212.000000" "75.380000"  "4.962500"  

iris <- tibble::as_tibble(iris)

# All numeric columns, but not the factor:
restore_zeros_df(iris)
#> Warning: `restore_zeros_df()` was deprecated in scrutiny 1.0.0.
#> ℹ Give the number of decimal places as `digits_x` or `digits_sd` instead. To
#>   format numbers for display, use `formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)`.
#> # A tibble: 150 × 5
#>    Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
#>    <chr>        <chr>       <chr>        <chr>       <fct>  
#>  1 5.1          3.5         1.4          0.2         setosa 
#>  2 4.9          3.0         1.4          0.2         setosa 
#>  3 4.7          3.2         1.3          0.2         setosa 
#>  4 4.6          3.1         1.5          0.2         setosa 
#>  5 5.0          3.6         1.4          0.2         setosa 
#>  6 5.4          3.9         1.7          0.4         setosa 
#>  7 4.6          3.4         1.4          0.3         setosa 
#>  8 5.0          3.4         1.5          0.2         setosa 
#>  9 4.4          2.9         1.4          0.2         setosa 
#> 10 4.9          3.1         1.5          0.1         setosa 
#> # ℹ 140 more rows

# Selected columns:
restore_zeros_df(iris, starts_with("Sepal"), width = 3)
#> # A tibble: 150 × 5
#>    Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
#>    <chr>        <chr>              <dbl>       <dbl> <fct>  
#>  1 5.100        3.500                1.4         0.2 setosa 
#>  2 4.900        3.000                1.4         0.2 setosa 
#>  3 4.700        3.200                1.3         0.2 setosa 
#>  4 4.600        3.100                1.5         0.2 setosa 
#>  5 5.000        3.600                1.4         0.2 setosa 
#>  6 5.400        3.900                1.7         0.4 setosa 
#>  7 4.600        3.400                1.4         0.3 setosa 
#>  8 5.000        3.400                1.5         0.2 setosa 
#>  9 4.400        2.900                1.4         0.2 setosa 
#> 10 4.900        3.100                1.5         0.1 setosa 
#> # ℹ 140 more rows
